payload.detail: CONFIRMED BY A LIVE READ 2026-09-17/18 — this row was raised as INFERRED FROM CODE AND CI EVIDENCE, NOT FROM A LIVE READ, and its stated next action was to read the live site_content_releases row. That read has now been done and it confirms the row: public.site_content_releases holds exactly ONE release, e4a1dd29-14f6-556c-8fb7-f4f947d8b846, state=active, created 2026-09-11, expected_record_count 843 and 843 actual rows, release_digest 57f6ec90... That is the 2026-08-24 epoch-zero freeze, and site_content_sync_state reports initialized=false with change_epoch 0. Breakdown of the 843 by kind: 330 medications, 232 differentials, 227 services, 54 forms. The repository catalogue carries 244 services, so the 17 service records added by PR #2814 are in the repository and NOT in the database. THE CLINICAL CONCERN IS THEREFORE REAL: service contact details and eligibility corrected since 2026-08-24 are not what the database serves. PARTIALLY MITIGATED, NOT CLOSED, by PR #2861: universal search and the registry list route now top up from the in-repo catalogue while the served release is still a retained bootstrap, so the 17 records — including SARC, 1800RESPECT, StandBy, Thirrili, Culture Care Connect, ARBOR, CYPRESS and the Aftercare Services Program — are findable again and are pinned to validationStatus unverified so they can never carry a sign-off. That is a stopgap which switches itself off the moment a real release is activated; it publishes nothing. CLOSING THIS STILL REQUIRES THE PUBLICATION. Its size is now measured rather than guessed — see PR #2872: 222 service groups, each with exactly ONE candidate and ONE distinct content hash, so the review is one policy decision plus 11 individual records (8 published with no owner row, 3 owner rows never published), not 222 judgements.
